summary: The FCC comment opposes changes to E-Rate that could limit noneducational screen use during school hours and require recipients to implement internet safety policies and privacy protections. The comment cites evidence from psychological and public health studies showing the negative effects of screen time and noneducational content on children's academic achievement and mental health. The comment also highlights recent legal cases that reinforce the need for enforceable rules to protect children The text argues against tying E-Rate decisions to educational outcomes and emphasizes the importance of connecting children to knowledge while avoiding the conversion of their attention and data into revenue.
